links.comparator_used: Inter-clinician agreement among expert reviewers adjudicating the same flagged items (clinician-to-clinician envelope), since no gold standard exists
links.outcome: Agreement on whether flagged items were genuine documentation errors
links.effect: Judge-clinician agreement 64% (95% CI 60 to 68) vs inter-clinician raw agreement 59% (95% CI 50 to 67; AC1 0.24); pipeline concurred on 70% (95% CI 59 to 79) of 77 consensus items; kept-precision 74% for AI vs 81% for clinician notes
links.tradeoff: Judge is not shown to be accurate: moderate concordance on consensus cases and fair human reliability preclude an accuracy claim. One asymmetry: removed-confirmed 56% vs 42%, so the screen over-removes more on clinician notes. Genuine-error rate can only be reported as an interval (68%, 94% credible interval 48 to 83).
links.quote: Judge-clinician agreement was 64% (95% CI 60 to 68), overlapping that interval.

design_hint: validating automated LLM judges of documentation errors against blinded clinician adjudication
